ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Diarrhea limits adherence

A patient starts misoprostol for NSAID-associated gastric ulcer prevention. Within the first week, frequent loose stools and abdominal cramps develop without fever or bleeding. Which adverse effect most likely explains why he wants to stop treatment?

  1. Antimuscarinic ileus
  2. Bismuth-associated black stool
  3. Prostaglandin-mediated diarrhea
  4. Dopamine-blockade dystonia
  5. Aluminum-associated constipation
Answer and explanation

Prostaglandin-mediated diarrhea

Diarrhea and abdominal discomfort are common dose-related limitations of misoprostol.

Option explanations

Prostaglandin-mediated diarrhea: Diarrhea and abdominal discomfort are common dose-related limitations of misoprostol.

Dopamine-blockade dystonia: Dystonia is associated with dopamine antagonists.

Aluminum-associated constipation: Aluminum products tend to cause constipation.

Antimuscarinic ileus: Misoprostol is not antimuscarinic.

Bismuth-associated black stool: Bismuth can darken stool but does not explain this exposure.
